name: Maitri
location: Schirmacher Oasis, Queen Maud Land, East Antarctica
description: Maitri is India's second permanent research station in Antarctica, commissioned in 1989 in the ice-free rocky terrain of the Schirmacher Oasis. It serves as a vital inland polar hub for geological, atmospheric, geomagnetism, glaciological and biological studies with an adjoining freshwater lake, Lake Priyadarshini.
facilities: Maitri Main Complex (insulated living & laboratory modules)

name: Bharati
description: Bharati is India's state-of-the-art third Antarctic research station, commissioned in March 2012 between Thala Fjord and Quilty Bay in the Larsemann Hills. Constructed from 134 prefabricated shipping containers and elevated on stilts, it represents cutting-edge green polar architecture and fast satellite telemetry.
scienceFocus: Remote Sensing & High-Latitude Satellite Data Acquisition
facilities: ISRO Polar Satellite Telemetry Station (S/X-band receive station)
Dedicated Helipad and Logistics Staging Dock

name: Himadri
description: Himadri is India's premier Arctic research station situated at the world's northernmost scientific research community at Ny-Ålesund, Svalbard. Inaugurated in July 2008, Himadri provides Indian scientists with round-the-year access to explore Arctic atmospheric phenomena, fjord oceanography, and microbial diversity.
scienceFocus: Teleconnection between Arctic Sea-Ice and Indian Monsoon

name: Himansh
location: Chandra Basin, Lahaul-Spiti, Himachal Pradesh, India
description: Himansh (meaning 'a slice of ice') is India's high-altitude research station established by NCPOR in the Western Himalaya at an elevation of 4,080 meters (13,385 ft). It spearheads long-term glaciological monitoring across Sutri Dhaka, Batal, Samudra Tapu, and Gepang Gath glaciers.
scienceFocus: Black Carbon & Aerosol Deposition on Snow
Ground Penetrating Radar (GPR) Ice Thickness Mapping
facilities: Hydrometric Gauge Stations along Chandra River

name: Dakshin Gangotri
location: Princess Astrid Coast, Queen Maud Land, Antarctica
description: Dakshin Gangotri was India's first permanent scientific base station established in Antarctica in 1983 during the Third Indian Antarctic Expedition. Submerged under ice in 1990, it is preserved as an Antarctic historic site and now serves as a field resupply point.
